title: Selectable-field filters must be checked against what the index actually mapped
answers: Filter on a custom/selectable field returns zero results with no error
Why does a LIST with a field selector silently return nothing
Search filter on a newly declared selectable field matches nothing
How to refuse filters on fields the index doesn't have
body:
Symptom: a filter on a selectable field declared after the index was built silently matches zero objects, indistinguishable from a legitimate empty result.
Root cause: pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:toBleveSearchRequest turned the filter into an exact term query against a bleve field that was never mapped, so bleve just finds nothing.
Fix pattern: before building the query, compare requested selectable fields against the set the index was actually built with (read from build info at open time) and return a structured error (resource.NewSelectableFieldNotIndexedError) naming the unmapped fields instead of querying.
Constraints: applies to filters; sorting and faceting on selectable fields were already refused the same way. Only relevant because the index's mapped-field set can lag the live kind declarations (index rebuild in progress, or a separate search server process with an older index).
applies: pkg/storage/unified/search index query building for selectable fields
says: Filtering on a custom field silently returns zero results no error
Why does list filtering on a newly declared field find nothing?
Search filter on new selectable field matches zero resources
How do I handle filters on fields the search index lacks?
Field filter silently fails instead of reporting which fields missing
search: Selectable-field filters must be validated against the actual index mapping before building the query; pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:toBleveSearchRequest must compare requested fields against the set the index was built with and return resource.NewSelectableFieldNotIndexedError for unmapped fields instead of silently matching zero objects. The mismatch occurs when a selectable field is declared after index build or when an older search server process has a lagging index. Constraint: this validation applies to filters only; sorting and faceting on selectable fields were already refused the same way. Irrelevant if the index's mapped-field set is always current with live kind declarations.
